failures.planner_decision: SELECTED BUY_ANIMAL for COW, SHEEP, and GOOSE simultaneously in one planning cycle
failures.expected_value: sum of 3 independently-calibrated animal_production_value() estimates (~$13,273 combined)
failures.actual_outcome: no jointly-validated evidence exists for 3 simultaneous animal species -- F5/F6/F7 each
tested exactly ONE animal alongside a crop; a later full-episode run showed one of the
two purchased animals (COW) produced ZERO units while the other (SHEEP) produced 21,
consistent with real, previously-untested multi-animal labor contention
failures.root_cause: each BUY_ANIMAL candidate is evaluated independently by evaluator.py, with no model of
cross-candidate labor competition among multiple simultaneously-committed animals -- a
genuine economic_model gap (Phase 2.5's inventory flagged 'whether sub-additivity worsens
as animal count scales' as UNKNOWN; this is a direct instance of that exact gap)
failures.fix: capped total committed animals (across all species) at 2, matching the ONLY jointly-validated
multi-animal configuration (Phase 2.3 F13's GOOSE+COW pair) -- enforced in both
agents/phase2_6/decisions.py (cross-lane cap during selection, since each species is its own
lane and per-lane independence alone doesn't prevent 3 simultaneous purchases)
failures.regression_test: not yet automated as a regression test (the fix is structural/capacity-based,
verified by direct trace inspection during development, not a scripted assertion) --
flagged as a Phase 2.6 limitation, not silently left unfixed
failures.outcome: FIXED (the cap), but the UNDERLYING labor-contention-among-multiple-animals question
remains genuinely UNKNOWN and unresolved -- documented, not fabricated an answer for

failures.planner_decision: SELECTED 'hire hand #1' repeatedly, every single day, never progressing to hand #2/#3
failures.expected_value: N/A -- this was a candidate-generation bug, not a valuation error
failures.actual_outcome: n_hands never grew past 1 in the tactical execution layer despite the planner
believing it had committed to increasing hands
failures.root_cause: opportunities.py and evaluator.py originally read `state.n_hands` (freshly adapted from
`obs` at the exact day-boundary planning moment) to decide which hand-count to propose
next -- but hands are cleared every day by design (VERIFIED, kaggriculture.py::
_end_of_day), so `state.n_hands` is STRUCTURALLY always 0 at that exact moment,
regardless of any previously-committed target. This is a state-representation error:
conflating the momentarily-OBSERVED value with the planner's own COMMITTED target.
failures.fix: opportunities.py and evaluator.py now read the committed target from `current_config['n_hands']`
instead of `state.n_hands` when generating/evaluating HIRE_HAND/REDUCE_HANDS candidates
failures.regression_test: not yet automated as a dedicated regression test (caught and fixed via smoke-test
trace inspection); the general determinism/candidate-generation tests in
scripts/phase2_6_regression_tests.py would not have caught this specific class of
bug -- flagged as a real gap in current test coverage
failures.outcome: FIXED, verified via smoke test (hand #1 then hand #2 correctly proposed on subsequent cycles)
